account:
Today I have kept my appointments, inspected the mill stall, visited my neighbour for tea, and returned to the office. The mill stall contained ninety-eight hay blocks when I inspected it, but that does not establish the town's full grain supply. The secretary reports no correspondence or council business awaiting attention. The innkeeper has arrived early for our 17:45 office appointment; we are due in the great hall at 18:00 to discuss the inn's service to town. I have welcomed the innkeeper and offered to hear any preliminary business.

The unusual matter is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk mentioned the baker, innkeeper, and someone called freight in connection with it. I have not witnessed such a change or obtained a firsthand explanation. My neighbour also heard the rumours but crossed the bridge without trouble. The baker advertised fresh bread this afternoon, which is ordinary business and does not explain the reports. I cannot yet tell whether the reported change concerns access, deliveries, or something else, nor what it is for. The innkeeper may be able to clarify, but involvement in neighbours' reports is not proof of any particular action or purpose.
